definition: Model output constrained to follow a specific, machine-readable format (such as JSON) rather than free-form natural language text.
details: Structured output is essential for reliably integrating LLMs into software systems, since downstream code typically needs to parse the model's response programmatically.

explainer.lead: Model output constrained to a specific, machine-readable format such as JSON rather than free-form natural language text. It matters because downstream code usually needs to parse the model's response programmatically.

tiers.eli5: The model writes its answer in a tidy labelled box instead of a paragraph, so a computer can pick out each field without guessing.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to reliably integrate LLMs into software systems; the pitfall is treating an unconstrained response as if it were already parseable.
tiers.paperLevel: Model output is constrained to follow a specific, machine-readable format (such as JSON) rather than free-form natural language text.

explainer.example: A model returns a JSON object with named fields instead of a prose paragraph, so software can read each value directly.
